text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Slovakia's charge d'affaires to Peru Julius Grancak is among the hostages being held by Peruvian guerrillas in the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima.
- Slovakia has announced a tender for the licence to operate one of two terrestrial TV channels currently run by the official Slovak Television.
- Parliament on February 15 will continue to discuss an opposition proposal on a change of the election of the president from a two-thirds parliamentary majority to a direct popular vote.

- Opposition parties said they would start collecting signatures to initiate a referendum on the change in the system for the election of the president early next year. According to Slovak law, 350,000 signatures are required to call a referendum.

- U.S. fast food chain McDonalds' said it planned to double its Slovak outlets to eight by the end of next year. McDonalds' has so far invested 150 million crowns into building its four Slovak outlets.
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Slovakia's highway network should be completed by the year 2005, when the total network should be 660 kilometres, compared with the current 215 kilometres.
- The Centre for Economic Development, an independent Slovak economic think tank, has warned that the current form of privatisation, mainly by direct sales, can slow down Slovakia's economic growth.
- Export-Import company Petrimex a.s., specialising mainly in trade with petrochemical products and materials, said it planned a gross profit of 65 to 70 million crowns this year.
